$comment: Numbers in a Kotlin value written into HTML, judged by both editors alike: an unsigned number is not a kotlin.Number, so interpolate refuses it where only a number is let in; a declared Number, and a call to toLong() or toInt() on a whole value, is a number; a number that may be null is said to be one. A case may give `constants`, the workspace's const val names.

cases.name: a number joined with + into a DSL expression is safe
cases.source:
import io.github.markusaugust.streamlord.html.*
fun f(id: Int) = elements { div { dataOnClick("@get('/x/" + id + "')") } }

cases.name: a number that may be null in style is said to be one

issues.message: Kotlin writes ${w} into style, where it is read as CSS, so escaping does not help. It is a number that may be null, which Kotlin writes as null: give it a value with ?:, or choose between classes.

cases.name: a number that may be null in text says nothing
a UInt in data-signals: interpolate always throws, a UInt is not a Number
cases.source:
import io.github.markusaugust.streamlord.core.domain.interpolate fun f(u: UInt) = interpolate("""

""", u)

issues.message: interpolate always throws here: u is an unsigned number, which is not a kotlin.Number, and it lands in data-signals, which Datastar runs as an expression or follows as a signal path, where only a number or a boolean is let in. Convert it with toLong() first.
fixes:
import io.github.markusaugust.streamlord.core.domain.interpolate fun f(u: UInt) = interpolate("""

""", u.toLong())

cases.name: a ULong in style: interpolate always throws
cases.source:
import io.github.markusaugust.streamlord.core.domain.interpolate fun f(w: ULong) = interpolate("""

""", w)

issues.message: interpolate always throws here: w is an unsigned number, which is not a kotlin.Number, and it lands in style, which is read as CSS, where only a number is let in. Convert it with toLong() first.
fixes:
import io.github.markusaugust.streamlord.core.domain.interpolate fun f(w: ULong) = interpolate("""

""", w.toLong())

cases.name: an unsigned literal in data-signals: interpolate always throws

issues.message: interpolate always throws here: 5u is an unsigned number, which is not a kotlin.Number, and it lands in data-signals, which Datastar runs as an expression or follows as a signal path, where only a number or a boolean is let in. Convert it with toLong() first.

cases.name: a UInt written by Kotlin: digits, but interpolate would refuse it in data-signals and style

issues.message: Kotlin writes ${u} into data-signals as digits, which is safe there, but it is an unsigned number, which interpolate refuses there: it is not a kotlin.Number. Convert it with toLong() if you build this with interpolate.

Kotlin writes ${u} into style as digits, which is safe there, but it is an unsigned number, which interpolate refuses there: it is not a kotlin.Number. Convert it with toLong() if you build this with interpolate.

a UInt converted with toLong() is a number

""", u.toLong())

cases.name: a sum converted with toInt() is a number

""", (a + b).toInt())

cases.name: a safe call to toLong() may be null
cases.source:
import io.github.markusaugust.streamlord.core.domain.* fun f(u: UInt?) = interpolate("""

""", u?.toLong())

issues.message: interpolate throws here unless u?.toLong() is a number or a boolean: it lands in data-signals, which Datastar runs as an expression or follows as a signal path. Put the value in an attribute of its own, such as data-label, and read it in the expression with el.dataset.label.

cases.name: a sum that ends in toInt() is not known to be a number
cases.source:
import io.github.markusaugust.streamlord.core.domain.* fun f(s: String, u: UInt) = interpolate("""

""", s + u.toInt())

issues.message: interpolate throws here unless s + u.toInt() is a number: it lands in style, which is read as CSS. Pass a number and write the unit in the markup, or choose between classes.
